## Virtual machines

### virt-manager and KVM {#kvm}

A Windows 11 VM with VirtIO and SPICE

- **Guide:** [Virt-Manager / KVM]({{< relref "/docs/virtualization/vm-setup" >}})
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3530-L3532) · [`on_kvm`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3072-L3085) · [`off_kvm`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3088-L3099)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar virt-manager qemu-full swtpm edk2-ovmf dnsmasq

# Set up libvirt: your account, the service, the default network
usermod --append --groups libvirt your-username
systemctl enable --now libvirtd
virsh net-start default || true
virsh net-autostart default

# Let VMs reach DNS and DHCP through ufw
ufw allow in on virbr0 to any port 53 proto udp comment 'VM DNS'
ufw allow in on virbr0 to any port 67 proto udp comment 'VM DHCP'
ufw route allow in on virbr0
ufw route allow out on virbr0
```

- Needs logging out and back in: the libvirt group.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Stop libvirt, its default network and take your account out of the libvirt group
virsh net-autostart --disable default || true
virsh net-destroy default || true
systemctl disable --now libvirtd || true
gpasswd -d your-username libvirt || true

# Take the VM rules out of ufw again
ufw --force delete allow in on virbr0 to any port 53 proto udp || true
ufw --force delete allow in on virbr0 to any port 67 proto udp || true
ufw --force route delete allow in on virbr0 || true
ufw --force route delete allow out on virbr0 || true

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar virt-manager
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar qemu-full
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar swtpm
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar edk2-ovmf
```

- Your virtual machines and their disks in /var/lib/libvirt stay where they are.
- Kept, because other things use them: dnsmasq
- Needs logging out and back in: leaving the libvirt group.

### VirtIO drivers ISO {#virtio-iso}

The Windows guest drivers, about 880 MB

- **Guide:** [Virt-Manager / KVM]({{< relref "/docs/virtualization/vm-setup" >}})
- **Needs:** [virt-manager and KVM](#kvm)
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3533-L3534) · [`on_virtio_iso`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3115-L3126) · [`off_virtio_iso`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3129-L3131)

Ticking it also ticks what it needs.

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Download the VirtIO drivers ISO (about 880 MB)
mkdir -p /var/lib/libvirt/images
curl -fL --proto '=https' -o /var/lib/libvirt/images/virtio-win.iso.part https://fedorapeople.org/groups/virt/virtio-win/direct-downloads/stable-virtio/virtio-win.iso
[ "$(stat -c %s /var/lib/libvirt/images/virtio-win.iso.part)" -gt 700000000 ] || { rm -f /var/lib/libvirt/images/virtio-win.iso.part; echo 'The download is incomplete'; exit 1; }
mv -f /var/lib/libvirt/images/virtio-win.iso.part /var/lib/libvirt/images/virtio-win.iso
```

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Delete the VirtIO drivers ISO
rm -f /var/lib/libvirt/images/virtio-win.iso /var/lib/libvirt/images/virtio-win.iso.part
```

### Quickemu {#quickemu}

Throwaway VMs in two commands

- **Guide:** [Quickemu]({{< relref "/docs/virtualization/quickemu" >}})
- **Marked:** `AUR`
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3535-L3536)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As you, in a terminal window ---

# Install from the AUR: paru shows each PKGBUILD, and you read it before it builds
paru -S --needed quickemu
```

From the AUR unless a repository you use carries the package: then it is the `pacman` line.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar quickemu
```

### VMware Workstation {#vmware}

Best VM performance. Builds kernel modules, so it needs DKMS and your kernel's headers

- **Guide:** [VMware Workstation]({{< relref "/docs/virtualization/vmware-workstation" >}})
- **Marked:** `Advanced`, `AUR`
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3540-L3543) · [`on_vmware`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3233-L3245) · [`off_vmware`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3248-L3252)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar dkms linux-cachyos-headers

# --- As you, in a terminal window ---

# Install from the AUR: paru shows each PKGBUILD, and you read it before it builds
paru -S --needed vmware-workstation

# --- As you ---

# Enable the VMware networking service (one more password prompt)
pkexec systemctl enable --now vmware-networks.service
```

- Needs a reboot: VMware's kernel modules (vmmon, vmnet).

From the AUR unless a repository you use carries the package: then it is the `pacman` line.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Stop the VMware services
systemctl disable --now vmware-networks.service || true
systemctl disable --now vmware.service || true

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar vmware-workstation
```

- DKMS and the kernel headers stay: other kernel modules (NVIDIA) use them. Your virtual machines stay.

### VMware keyboard fix for GNOME Wayland {#vmware-keyboard}

Lets VMware grab the keyboard through XWayland. Needed on GNOME 49, untested on newer

- **Guide:** [VMware Workstation]({{< relref "/docs/virtualization/vmware-workstation" >}}#gnome-49-wayland-keyboard-grab)
- **Needs:** [VMware Workstation](#vmware)
- **Only on:** the GNOME desktop
- **Marked:** `Advanced`
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3544-L3547) · [`on_vmware_keyboard`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3266-L3269) · [`off_vmware_keyboard`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3272-L3275)

Ticking it also ticks what it needs.

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Set xwayland-allow-grabs
gsettings set org.gnome.mutter.wayland xwayland-allow-grabs true

# Set xwayland-grab-access-rules
gsettings set org.gnome.mutter.wayland xwayland-grab-access-rules "['vmware', 'vmware-vmx']"
```

- Needs logging out and back in: the VMware keyboard fix.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Reset xwayland-allow-grabs
gsettings reset org.gnome.mutter.wayland xwayland-allow-grabs

# Reset xwayland-grab-access-rules
gsettings reset org.gnome.mutter.wayland xwayland-grab-access-rules
```

- Needs logging out and back in: undoing the VMware keyboard fix.

## Containers

### Podman and Podman Desktop {#podman}

Rootless containers with a docker-compatible CLI

- **Guide:** [Development]({{< relref "/docs/applications/development" >}}#podman--podman-desktop)
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3548-L3551) · [`on_podman`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3041-L3046) · [`off_podman`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3049-L3052) · [`podman_on_blocker`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3017-L3021)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar podman podman-docker podman-desktop

# Silence the 'Emulate Docker CLI' notice
touch /etc/containers/nodocker

# Let short image names resolve through docker.io and ghcr.io
mkdir -p /etc/containers/registries.conf.d
cat > /etc/containers/registries.conf.d/99-zephyrus-search.conf <<'ZEPHYRUS_EOF'
unqualified-search-registries = ["docker.io", "ghcr.io"]
ZEPHYRUS_EOF
```

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Remove the Podman settings this script added
rm -f /etc/containers/nodocker /etc/containers/registries.conf.d/99-zephyrus-search.conf

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar podman
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar podman-docker
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar podman-desktop
```

- Your containers, images and volumes stay in your home folder.
